Page38 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version Figure 3.14: LPG Handling Assets Adjacent to T-RICH Site 3.8.2 AMMONIA The threat of toxic exposure exists from ammonia vapor leakage from the nearby Tampa Ammonia Terminal (NH ). Based on the apparent tank configuration at the Ammonia Terminal, it is assumed that 3 the ammonia is being stored at or near atmospheric pressure just below its boiling point of approximately -33 °C which is a typical terminal storage design. This makes a large breach of a tank "unlikely" and will be a low-pressure release. Ammonia is a gas at atmospheric pressure and temperatures above its boiling point (-33°C). Its flash point is 11°C, and it has a relative density in air of ~0.7 and a molar mass of 17.03 g/mol. Ammonia becomes a flammable mixture in air at concentrations of 15% (LFL) to 28% (UFL) and is highly toxic to humans. The Ammonia Terminal has a leak "area notification system" as part of the Port of Tampa Emergency Response Program. This system is briefly summarized in Section 3.7. The Ammonia Terminal is located approximately 1,000 feet north (see Fig. 3.15). While the risk of toxic exposure levels needs to be understood, it is likely that the "area notification system," combined with appropriate training and procedures, and the planned provision of CO leakage "shelter(s) in place" (See Section 8.3.5) at the T- 2 RICH site will likely be determined to be sufficient to address the risk of worker exposure to ammonia. However, a detailed review of any existing Facility Siting Study or Major Process Hazard Analysis documentation that should exist for the Ammonia Terminal property and operations should be undertaken in order to verify the above assumptions. Page39 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version Figure 3.15: Ammonia Terminal Relative to T-RICH Site 3.9 FUTURE EXPANSION The initial equipment and infrastructure layout for T-RICH (See Section 4.5) takes up only 8.5 acres of the total 16± acres within the available parcel. As can be seen, there is an additional 7.5± acres on the east side of the site that can be used for future expansion. It was found that T-RICH can be expanded by utilizing one of the following two options: Option 1: Add 9 more storage tanks, for 20 total, and two more sets of 50% liquefaction trains for an increased annual throughput of 6mtpa. See Figure 3.16. Option 2: Add 9 more storage tanks as in Option 1, but change the arrangement of the liquefaction trains to make them more compact. This change in liquefaction trains allows for an ultimate throughput increase to 8 mpta. See Figure 3.17. With Option 1, the plot plan depicted herein can be built and commissioned to support the initial anticipated 2mtpa throughput.
